quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Vocational training partnerships between community colleges and regional employers are structured so that curriculum content is jointly designed by faculty and industry representatives, rather than developed unilaterally by either party in isolation. Workforce development researchers credit this approach with producing graduates whose skills more closely match immediate employer needs than graduates of conventionally designed programs. Yet this very responsiveness to current employer specifications introduces a longer-term vulnerability that the same researchers are careful to note: curricula optimized tightly around a particular employer's present-day technical requirements risk leaving graduates narrowly prepared for equipment or processes that employer may substantially revise within a few years. This is a trade-off between immediate employability and longer-term adaptability that no single partnership structure studied so far has managed to resolve cleanly, since strengthening one side of the trade-off through closer employer involvement appears to come reliably at some cost to the other.
options: Employer-Aligned Training Trading Long-Term Adaptability for Immediate Employability
Employer-Designed Curricula Confirmed to Improve Both Immediate and Long-Term Outcomes
Researchers Found No Trade-Off Between Employer Involvement and Graduate Adaptability
Conventionally Designed Programs Found to Match Employer Needs More Closely
quests.correctAnswer: Employer-Aligned Training Trading Long-Term Adaptability for Immediate Employability
quests.hint: Notice the two different outcomes compared, immediate employability and longer-term adaptability, and why strengthening one appears to come at the expense of the other.
quests.explanation: This passage combines the genuine immediate-employability benefit of close employer involvement with a longer-term adaptability cost that researchers say no partnership structure has resolved. The summary should capture that unresolved trade-off rather than present employer-aligned curricula as straightforwardly superior.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Performance-based pay structures for sales employees, in which compensation is weighted heavily toward commission earned on completed sales rather than a stable base salary, are typically justified by employers on the grounds that such structures align individual incentive directly with desired business outcomes more precisely than salary-based compensation can. Organizational behavior researchers studying long-term effects on customer relationships, though, have found that heavily commission-weighted structures can incentivize behavior that maximizes short-term transaction closure at the expense of the kind of longer-term customer relationship maintenance, follow-up support, and honest product-fit assessment that ultimately drives repeat business and referrals. The very incentive alignment commission structures are designed to achieve, in other words, may apply cleanly only to the narrow, immediate sales metric being directly compensated, while working against the broader, harder-to-measure outcomes the business genuinely depends on for sustained success.
options: Commission Structures Confirmed to Improve Both Immediate Sales and Long-Term Relationships
Commission Incentives Aligning with Immediate Sales but Undermining Broader Business Goals
Heavily Commission-Weighted Pay Found to Have No Effect on Customer Relationship Quality
Researchers Found Salary-Based Compensation to Produce Identical Incentive Effects
quests.correctAnswer: Commission Incentives Aligning with Immediate Sales but Undermining Broader Business Goals
quests.hint: Consider the specific, narrow outcome commission structures successfully incentivize compared to the broader business outcomes these same structures can work against.
quests.explanation: This passage brings together the precise incentive alignment commission structures achieve for immediate sales with the broader relationship costs that same alignment can produce. The summary should capture that narrow-versus-broad tension rather than present commission pay as uniformly aligned with business success.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: International student exchange programs are frequently promoted on the premise that direct, sustained cross-cultural contact reliably reduces participants' prejudice and increases intercultural understanding. Research findings complicate this premise considerably. Contact alone, absent specific structural conditions identified by intergroup contact researchers, including equal status between groups during the contact, cooperative rather than competitive interaction structure, and sufficient duration to move beyond superficial interaction, does not reliably produce the hoped-for attitude change. Contact occurring under conditions lacking these features has in some documented cases reinforced rather than reduced pre-existing stereotypes, since negative or superficial interactions can be interpreted as confirming prior assumptions just as readily as positive interactions can be interpreted as disconfirming them. Program design specifics, in short, matter considerably more than the mere fact of cross-cultural contact occurring.
options: Cross-Cultural Contact Confirmed to Reliably Reduce Prejudice Under Any Circumstances
Superficial or Negative Contact Found to Reduce Stereotypes as Effectively as Positive Contact
Cross-Cultural Contact Reducing Prejudice Only Under Specific Structural Conditions
Researchers Found Program Design Specifics Make No Difference to Contact Outcomes
quests.correctAnswer: Cross-Cultural Contact Reducing Prejudice Only Under Specific Structural Conditions
quests.hint: Think about the specific structural conditions identified as necessary for cross-cultural contact to actually reduce prejudice, and what happens when contact occurs without those conditions.
quests.explanation: This passage links the popular premise behind exchange programs with research showing contact only works under specific structural conditions, and can backfire without them. The summary should capture that conditional, design-dependent finding rather than confirm contact alone as sufficient.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Inheritance tax policy debates frequently center on competing intuitions about fairness that prove difficult to reconcile through empirical evidence alone. One prominent position holds that wealth transferred across generations without having been earned by the recipient through their own labor or merit represents a legitimate target for taxation, precisely because it perpetuates unearned advantage. An opposing position holds that wealth already taxed once as income during the original earner's lifetime should not face a second layer of taxation merely because of the timing and method of its eventual transfer to heirs. This is a genuine disagreement rooted in differing underlying values about the proper basis of fair taxation, rather than in any disputed factual question that additional economic research could straightforwardly resolve, meaning policy debate in this area tends to recur without clear resolution not from any lack of available data but from this deeper, persistent values disagreement.
options: The Inheritance Tax Debate Confirmed to Stem from a Disputed Factual Question
Additional Economic Research Found Capable of Resolving This Policy Disagreement
Both Sides of the Debate Found to Share Identical Underlying Values About Taxation
Inheritance Tax Debate Rooted in Unresolvable Values Disagreement, Not Missing Facts
quests.correctAnswer: Inheritance Tax Debate Rooted in Unresolvable Values Disagreement, Not Missing Facts
quests.hint: Look at whether the disagreement over inheritance tax is actually about disputed facts or about something else entirely, according to the passage's own framing.
quests.explanation: This passage explicitly frames the inheritance tax debate as rooted in differing values rather than disputed facts, explaining why it recurs without resolution despite available data. The summary should capture that values-based framing rather than suggest the disagreement is empirical or already resolved.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Grocery store layout design has long been optimized by retailers to maximize the distance and time customers spend traversing the store before reaching frequently purchased staple items typically positioned toward the rear. This exploits a behavioral pattern in which additional time spent walking past other merchandise correlates with additional impulse purchases beyond the original shopping list, a dynamic retailers have refined considerably through data on customer movement patterns. This same layout philosophy, though, has come under reconsideration in some stores serving customers for whom mobility limitations or time constraints make extended store traversal a genuine burden rather than a marketing opportunity. This has prompted a small number of retailers to experiment with express-format stores explicitly prioritizing rapid staple-item access over impulse-purchase-maximizing layout, a format that sacrifices average transaction value per visit in exchange for serving a customer segment whose loyalty depends on minimizing rather than extending in-store time.
options: Express-Format Stores Confirmed to Maximize Both Convenience and Impulse Purchases
Traditional Layout Philosophy Found to Serve Mobility-Limited Customers Equally Well
Retailers Found No Trade-Off Between Transaction Value and Customer Convenience
Express Store Formats Trading Impulse Revenue for an Underserved Customer Segment
quests.correctAnswer: Express Store Formats Trading Impulse Revenue for an Underserved Customer Segment
quests.hint: Ask yourself about the trade-off between traditional layout's impulse-purchase benefit and the express format's appeal to a specific customer segment, and what each format sacrifices to achieve its goal.
quests.explanation: This passage connects the traditional impulse-maximizing layout strategy with an emerging alternative format that sacrifices that same revenue advantage to better serve customers burdened by extended store time. The summary should capture that genuine trade-off between formats rather than suggest one approach serves all customers equally well.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Recipe standardization across regional or international restaurant chains is intended to ensure a consistent customer experience regardless of which specific location a customer visits. It confronts an inherent tension with ingredient sourcing realities, since achieving genuinely identical flavor profiles across geographically dispersed locations often requires either importing specific ingredients across considerable distances at substantial cost and environmental impact, or accepting some degree of flavor variation arising from regional differences in locally available ingredient quality, even when the written recipe and preparation procedure remain nominally identical. This tension has led some chains to quietly embrace a more flexible standardization approach, specifying target flavor outcomes and acceptable variation ranges rather than rigid universal ingredient lists. This adaptation preserves brand consistency at the level customers actually perceive, while reducing the logistical and environmental costs of pursuing literal ingredient uniformity across every location.
options: Rigid Ingredient Standardization Confirmed to Have No Cost or Logistical Impact
Flexible Standardization Balancing Brand Consistency Against Sourcing Costs
Flavor Variation Found to Be Eliminated Entirely Once Recipes Are Standardized
Customers Found to Perceive No Difference Between Rigid and Flexible Standardization Approaches
quests.correctAnswer: Flexible Standardization Balancing Brand Consistency Against Sourcing Costs
quests.hint: Identify the tension between achieving identical flavor everywhere and the practical costs of doing so, and what alternative approach some chains adopted to balance both concerns.
quests.explanation: This passage weaves together the tension between literal ingredient uniformity and its real costs with an adaptive solution focusing on perceived outcome rather than rigid process. The summary should capture that balanced resolution rather than suggest standardization is costless or that flexible approaches sacrifice perceived consistency.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Federated learning is a machine learning training approach in which a model is trained across numerous decentralized devices, each using locally held data that never leaves the device itself, with only resulting model updates, rather than raw underlying data, being shared back to a central coordinating server. It has been promoted as a privacy-preserving alternative to conventional centralized training approaches that require pooling raw user data in one location. Privacy researchers studying federated learning's actual guarantees, however, note that model updates themselves, despite not containing raw data directly, can under certain conditions be analyzed to partially reconstruct or infer sensitive characteristics of the underlying local training data, through techniques like gradient inversion. Federated learning, in other words, meaningfully reduces but does not entirely eliminate the privacy risk inherent in any system where information derived from sensitive data, even indirectly, is transmitted beyond the device where that data originally resides.
options: Federated Learning Confirmed to Eliminate All Privacy Risk Entirely
Model Updates Found to Contain No Information Derivable from Local Training Data
Federated Learning Reducing but Not Eliminating Privacy Risk Through Indirect Data Leakage
Gradient Inversion Techniques Found to Be Incapable of Inferring Any Sensitive Characteristics
quests.correctAnswer: Federated Learning Reducing but Not Eliminating Privacy Risk Through Indirect Data Leakage
quests.hint: Focus on what federated learning actually shares between devices and a central server, and what researchers have found can still be partially inferred from that shared information despite the absence of raw data.
quests.explanation: This passage draws together the genuine privacy improvement federated learning offers over centralized training with a documented residual risk from techniques that can partially infer data from shared model updates. The summary should capture that the protection is meaningful but incomplete, not absolute or absent.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Wearable health-tracking devices estimate metrics like sleep stages or stress levels through indirect physiological proxies, such as heart rate variability and movement patterns, rather than through direct measurement of the underlying physiological process itself. This has drawn scrutiny from sleep and physiology researchers comparing consumer device output against clinical-grade measurement equipment, since it introduces an inherent accuracy ceiling. Studies find that while these devices generally distinguish reasonably well between broad categories, such as being asleep versus awake, their more granular claims, such as precisely quantifying time spent in specific sleep stages or assigning a single numerical stress score, show considerably weaker correlation with clinical measurement. This gap between marketed precision and actual measurement validity matters because users may make health or lifestyle decisions based on granular metrics the underlying technology is not actually capable of measuring with the precision its presentation to users implies.
options: Wearables' Granular Health Metrics Less Valid Than Their Precise Presentation Implies
Wearable Devices Confirmed to Measure Granular Sleep Stages with Clinical-Grade Precision
Broad Sleep-Wake Classification Found to Be Less Accurate Than Granular Stage Measurement
Researchers Found No Gap Between Marketed Precision and Actual Device Validity
quests.correctAnswer: Wearables' Granular Health Metrics Less Valid Than Their Precise Presentation Implies
quests.hint: Picture the difference between how well these devices perform on broad classifications versus more granular, precise-sounding metrics, and why that gap matters for users making decisions.
quests.explanation: This passage balances reasonable device accuracy for broad categories against weaker validity for granular, precisely presented metrics, explaining why this gap matters for user decision-making. The summary should capture that specific distinction rather than treat all device outputs as equally reliable or unreliable.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Audience measurement methodology for television and streaming content has historically relied on relatively small representative panels of households, whose viewing behavior was extrapolated to estimate total national audience figures. This approach has faced growing methodological challenges as media consumption has fragmented across numerous platforms and devices in ways the original panel-based methodology was not designed to comprehensively capture. This has prompted a gradual industry shift toward measurement approaches incorporating actual aggregated viewing data directly from streaming platforms and smart television devices themselves. This transition, while offering considerably larger and more granular underlying data, introduces its own measurement challenges, including reconciling inconsistent definitions of what constitutes a counted 'view' across different platforms and devices. The industry, in other words, has traded one set of methodological limitations, panel size and representativeness, for a different set, definitional inconsistency across data sources, rather than arriving at a measurement approach free of any significant limitation.
options: The Shift to Aggregated Data Confirmed to Have Eliminated All Measurement Limitations
Audience Measurement Trading Panel Limitations for New Definitional Inconsistency Problems
Panel-Based Methodology Found to Have Comprehensively Captured Fragmented Media Consumption
Aggregated Viewing Data Found to Use Fully Consistent View Definitions Across All Platforms
quests.correctAnswer: Audience Measurement Trading Panel Limitations for New Definitional Inconsistency Problems
quests.hint: Compare the old panel-based measurement approach with the newer aggregated-data approach, and whether the newer approach actually solves every problem or just exchanges one set of problems for another.
quests.explanation: This passage unites the limitations of old panel-based measurement with the new, different limitations introduced by aggregated data approaches, concluding the industry traded one problem for another rather than achieving a flawless solution. The summary should capture that ongoing trade-off.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Automated translation tools embedded within messaging platforms enable real-time communication between speakers of different languages, without either party needing independent translation expertise, and have measurably expanded the practical scope of cross-linguistic personal and professional communication. Linguists studying actual usage patterns, though, note that current automated translation, however technically impressive its handling of literal semantic content, continues to struggle considerably with culturally specific idiom, indirect communication norms that vary meaningfully across cultures, and the subtle pragmatic cues, such as appropriate formality level inferred from context, that fluent human speakers navigate intuitively. Users relying exclusively on automated translation for genuinely important or relationally sensitive communication may therefore transmit literally accurate but pragmatically or socially inappropriate messages, without any signal from the tool itself that a translation, while semantically correct, has failed to capture something that actually mattered for the communication's real-world reception.
options: Automated Translation's Semantic Accuracy Masking Pragmatic and Cultural Gaps
Automated Translation Confirmed to Fully Capture Cultural and Pragmatic Nuance
Linguists Found No Limitations in How Translation Tools Handle Idiom or Formality
Users Found to Receive Clear Signals Whenever a Translation Misses Pragmatic Meaning
quests.correctAnswer: Automated Translation's Semantic Accuracy Masking Pragmatic and Cultural Gaps
quests.hint: Weigh the distinction between literal semantic accuracy and the pragmatic, cultural dimensions of communication, and what risk arises when a tool succeeds at one but silently fails at the other.
quests.explanation: This passage ties together the genuine expansion in cross-linguistic communication automated translation enables with its persistent, silent failure to capture pragmatic and cultural nuance. The summary should capture that specific risk of undetected miscommunication rather than suggest the technology fully succeeds or entirely fails.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Daily planning routines that prioritize tasks according to a fixed urgency-importance matrix, completing the most urgent and important tasks first before proceeding methodically to less pressing categories, are frequently recommended in popular productivity literature as a universally applicable approach to daily task management. Occupational researchers studying actual work patterns across different professional roles, however, have found this fixed sequencing approach poorly suited to roles characterized by frequent, genuinely unpredictable interruptions requiring immediate attention regardless of a worker's planned task order, such as many healthcare or emergency-response positions. Research instead supports a different planning approach for those roles, centered on maintaining flexible capacity reserves and rapid task-switching readiness rather than rigid sequential prioritization. The optimal planning framework, in other words, depends considerably on a role's actual interruption frequency and unpredictability, rather than representing a single universally optimal method applicable identically across all types of work.
options: A Fixed Urgency-Importance Matrix Confirmed to Be Universally Optimal Across All Professions
Healthcare and Emergency Roles Found to Benefit Most from Rigid Sequential Prioritization
Researchers Found Interruption Frequency Has No Bearing on Which Planning Method Works Best
Optimal Task Planning Depending on a Role's Interruption Frequency, Not One Universal Method
quests.correctAnswer: Optimal Task Planning Depending on a Role's Interruption Frequency, Not One Universal Method
quests.hint: Notice the specific factor identified as determining which planning approach actually works best for a given profession, rather than assuming one method suits every kind of work.
quests.explanation: This passage combines the popular universal planning recommendation with research showing its poor fit for high-interruption roles and a better-suited alternative for those roles, concluding the optimal method depends on interruption frequency. The summary should capture that role-dependent conclusion rather than endorse one universal method.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Cover letters accompanying job applications are traditionally expected to articulate a candidate's specific interest in a particular role and organization beyond what a standardized resume alone conveys. They have become subject to increasingly sophisticated detection efforts by hiring platforms attempting to identify letters generated largely or entirely by AI writing tools, a practice some applicants pursue believing a polished, professionally worded letter improves their candidacy regardless of its authorship. Hiring researchers studying recruiter response to detected AI-generated content have found a complicated picture, however. Recruiters report being unable to reliably distinguish AI-assisted from independently written letters through reading alone, meaning detection efforts increasingly rely on platform-level technical analysis rather than human judgment. At the same time, recruiters who learn a letter was AI-generated report this knowledge measurably lowering their assessment of a candidate's genuine interest in the role, even when the letter's actual content remains identical and was equally persuasive before its origin became known.
options: Recruiters Confirmed to Reliably Detect AI-Generated Letters Through Reading Alone
Knowledge of AI Authorship Found to Have No Effect on Recruiter Assessment
AI-Generated Letters Undetectable by Reading Alone, Yet Penalized Once Origin Is Known
Letter Content Found to Become Less Persuasive Once Recognized as AI-Generated
quests.correctAnswer: AI-Generated Letters Undetectable by Reading Alone, Yet Penalized Once Origin Is Known
quests.hint: Consider the two separate findings presented, recruiters' actual ability to detect AI authorship through reading versus how their assessment changes once that authorship is somehow revealed to them.
quests.explanation: This passage brings together recruiters' inability to detect AI-generated letters through reading alone with the separate finding that revealed AI authorship still lowers their assessment despite identical content. The summary should capture that combined, somewhat paradoxical pattern rather than suggest detection is easy or that disclosure has no consequence.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Corporate succession planning is the process by which organizations identify and develop internal candidates capable of eventually assuming senior leadership roles. It has historically concentrated developmental investment, mentorship access, and high-visibility project assignments on a relatively small group of employees identified early as 'high-potential.' Organizational researchers have increasingly criticized this practice on the grounds that early high-potential identification relies heavily on traits, such as confidence in client-facing presentation and willingness to self-promote internally, that correlate only loosely with actual long-term leadership effectiveness. Organizations following this conventional approach therefore risk simultaneously underinvesting in employees whose genuine leadership capability simply presents less visibly under early-career conditions, and overinvesting in employees whose early visibility reflects traits poorly predictive of how they will actually perform once given substantial organizational authority. Several organizations have begun addressing this mismatch between identification criteria and actual predictive validity through more structured, competency-based assessment occurring later in a candidate's career, when leadership-relevant behavior has had more opportunity to actually manifest.
options: Early High-Potential Identification Mismatched with What Actually Predicts Leadership
Early High-Potential Identification Confirmed to Strongly Predict Long-Term Leadership Success
Confidence and Self-Promotion Found to Correlate Strongly with Actual Leadership Effectiveness
Organizations Found No Need to Adjust Conventional Succession Planning Practices
quests.correctAnswer: Early High-Potential Identification Mismatched with What Actually Predicts Leadership
quests.hint: Think about the specific traits early high-potential identification typically relies on, and how well those traits actually predict genuine long-term leadership effectiveness.
quests.explanation: This passage links the conventional early-identification approach to succession planning with research showing a poor match between its selection criteria and actual leadership predictive validity, plus organizations' resulting shift toward later assessment. The summary should capture that mismatch and corrective response.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Long-haul flight scheduling decisions made by airlines balance passenger preference for convenient departure and arrival times against operational considerations like aircraft utilization efficiency and crew duty time regulations. Airlines have increasingly incorporated overnight 'red-eye' scheduling for routes where this was not previously common, a scheduling shift they justify primarily through aircraft utilization economics, since an aircraft flying overnight generates revenue during hours it would otherwise sit idle on the ground, rather than through any claim that passengers actually prefer overnight travel on these specific routes. This economically driven scheduling shift has prompted sleep researchers to raise concerns about cumulative circadian disruption among frequent business travelers who may take such overnight flights repeatedly, since the same circadian misalignment risks documented among shift workers performing irregular overnight schedules may apply similarly to frequent flyers. This population's travel-related sleep disruption has received comparatively less dedicated research attention than equivalent occupational shift-work disruption, despite plausibly similar underlying physiological mechanisms.
options: Red-Eye Scheduling Confirmed to Be Driven Primarily by Passenger Preference
Frequent Flyer Circadian Disruption Found to Have Received Equal Research Attention as Shift Work
Overnight Flight Scheduling Driven by Economics, Raising an Understudied Health Concern
Sleep Researchers Found No Plausible Connection Between Overnight Flights and Shift-Work Risks
quests.correctAnswer: Overnight Flight Scheduling Driven by Economics, Raising an Understudied Health Concern
quests.hint: Look at the actual reason airlines have shifted toward overnight scheduling, and the health concern this economically motivated shift has raised that has not yet received much dedicated research.
quests.explanation: This passage connects the genuine economic rationale behind increased red-eye scheduling with a raised but understudied health concern about cumulative circadian disruption for frequent travelers. The summary should capture both the economic driver and the research gap, rather than attribute the scheduling shift to passenger preference or dismiss the health concern.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Family businesses transitioning leadership from a founding generation to the next generation of family members face a documented pattern of elevated failure risk during the transition period itself. Business succession researchers attribute this vulnerability not primarily to any inherent deficiency in the incoming generation's competence, a common but largely unsupported assumption, but rather to a more structural set of challenges. These include the founding generation's frequent reluctance to fully relinquish decision-making authority even after a nominal leadership transition has formally occurred, ambiguity about whether non-family senior employees' career advancement prospects remain viable under family-dominated leadership structures, and the incoming generation's need to simultaneously establish independent credibility with employees, customers, and suppliers who may have related primarily to the previous leader personally. This combination of structural and relational challenges exists independent of, and considerably more consequential than, the incoming leader's individual capability.
options: Family Business Succession Failures Confirmed to Stem Primarily from Incoming Leader Incompetence
Family Business Transition Risk Stemming from Structural Factors, Not Incoming Leader Competence
Founding Generation Leaders Found to Readily Relinquish Decision-Making Authority After Transition
Non-Family Employees Found to Have No Concerns About Advancement Under New Leadership
quests.correctAnswer: Family Business Transition Risk Stemming from Structural Factors, Not Incoming Leader Competence
quests.hint: Ask yourself what business succession researchers actually identify as the main driver of failure risk during family business transitions, as distinguished from the common but unsupported assumption about the incoming generation's competence.
quests.explanation: This passage pairs the common but mistaken assumption about incoming-generation incompetence with the actual structural and relational factors researchers identify as the real drivers of transition risk. The summary should capture that corrected causal attribution rather than confirm the popular competence-based explanation.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Retail return policies offering extended return windows are ostensibly designed purely to enhance customer satisfaction and purchase confidence, by reducing the perceived risk of an unsatisfactory purchase. Retail economists, though, have examined these policies for a secondary, less publicly emphasized function. Extended return windows measurably increase the average time between initial purchase and final return decision, during which a meaningful proportion of customers simply forget about, lose the receipt for, or otherwise fail to complete an intended return they would have completed promptly under a shorter window. Extended return policies, in other words, can simultaneously serve the genuine customer-confidence function retailers emphasize publicly, while also functioning, whether by deliberate design or fortunate incidental effect, to reduce the practical return completion rate relative to what an equally generous but shorter-window policy might produce, a dual function retail economists note retailers rarely if ever acknowledge explicitly in customer-facing policy messaging.
options: Extended Return Windows Confirmed to Have Only the Single, Publicly Stated Customer Confidence Function
Longer Return Periods Found to Increase the Rate of Completed Returns
Retailers Found to Openly Acknowledge the Return-Reduction Effect in Their Marketing
Extended Return Windows Quietly Reducing Completed Returns While Boosting Confidence
quests.correctAnswer: Extended Return Windows Quietly Reducing Completed Returns While Boosting Confidence
quests.hint: Identify the publicly stated purpose of extended return windows compared to the secondary, less openly acknowledged effect regarding how many returns actually get completed.
quests.explanation: This passage weaves together the genuine, publicly emphasized customer-confidence benefit of extended return windows with an unstated secondary effect of reduced return completion due to forgetting. The summary should capture both functions rather than describe only the stated purpose or assume retailers openly admit the secondary effect.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Meal-delivery subscription services offering pre-portioned ingredients alongside step-by-step recipe instructions have been marketed substantially on a convenience and time-savings premise. Usability researchers tracking actual time spent by subscribers from package opening through final plated meal, however, have found that total preparation time frequently exceeds what equivalent supermarket-ingredient versions of similar recipes would require for an experienced home cook. Researchers attribute this counterintuitive finding to the services' instructional format being calibrated toward novice cooks requiring more detailed step-by-step guidance than an experienced cook would need. The services' actual time-saving value, in other words, depends considerably on a subscriber's baseline cooking skill level, offering genuine time efficiency primarily for novice cooks unfamiliar with the recipes' underlying techniques, while offering comparatively little or even negative time efficiency for already-skilled home cooks who could prepare equivalent dishes more quickly using their own existing technique and judgment.
options: Meal Kit Services Confirmed to Save Time Equally for Cooks of Every Skill Level
Experienced Cooks Found to Save More Time Using Meal Kits Than Novice Cooks
Meal Kit Time Savings Depending Heavily on a Subscriber's Existing Cooking Skill
Researchers Found No Relationship Between Cooking Skill and Meal Kit Time Efficiency
quests.correctAnswer: Meal Kit Time Savings Depending Heavily on a Subscriber's Existing Cooking Skill
quests.hint: Focus on why the time-saving benefit of meal kit services might actually depend on how experienced the cook already is.
quests.explanation: This passage draws together the marketed time-saving premise of meal kit services with research showing that benefit depends heavily on a subscriber's existing skill level, helping novices while offering little or negative benefit to experienced cooks. The summary should capture that skill-dependent variation rather than present the services as uniformly time-saving.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Smart home energy management systems, capable of automatically adjusting heating, cooling, and appliance scheduling based on factors including real-time electricity pricing, occupancy detection, and weather forecasting, have demonstrated measurable energy cost savings in controlled studies. Broader analysis of the technology's actual environmental benefit, though, reveals a more complicated picture than the marketed cost-savings figures alone suggest. The manufacturing footprint and ongoing energy consumption of the sensors, hubs, and connectivity infrastructure required to enable this automated optimization represent a genuine environmental cost that must be weighed against the operational energy savings the system subsequently produces. The technology's net environmental benefit, in other words, depends considerably on factors including how long a given system remains in service before replacement and how energy-intensive its specific manufacturing and connectivity requirements are, a full accounting that simple operational-savings marketing claims typically omit entirely.
options: Smart Home Systems Confirmed to Have No Manufacturing or Connectivity Energy Cost
Operational Energy Savings Found to Represent the Complete Environmental Picture
The Technology's Net Environmental Benefit Found to Be Unaffected by Device Lifespan
Smart Home Systems' Marketed Savings Omitting Their Own Manufacturing Energy Cost
quests.correctAnswer: Smart Home Systems' Marketed Savings Omitting Their Own Manufacturing Energy Cost
quests.hint: Picture what the marketed cost-savings figures for smart home systems typically leave out, and why that omission matters for understanding the technology's true net environmental benefit.
quests.explanation: This passage balances the demonstrated operational energy savings of smart home systems against the typically omitted manufacturing and connectivity energy costs required to enable those savings, concluding the net benefit depends on factors like device lifespan. The summary should capture that fuller, more complicated accounting rather than accept marketed savings figures at face value.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Telemedicine adoption for mental health treatment expanded considerably during recent years, driven partly by genuine clinical evidence supporting its effectiveness for many common conditions and partly by practical access improvements for patients facing geographic or mobility barriers to in-person care. Clinical researchers, though, have identified a meaningful subset of presentations, including certain acute crisis situations and conditions where a clinician's direct in-person observation of subtle nonverbal cues substantially informs diagnostic accuracy, for which telemedicine's reduced observational bandwidth relative to in-person assessment introduces genuine clinical limitations, rather than representing merely an equally effective alternative delivery format. This nuanced picture complicates both uncritical telemedicine enthusiasm, which tends to treat the format as a costless improvement applicable to all presentations, and reflexive telemedicine skepticism, which tends to discount the format's substantial genuine benefits for the considerably larger set of presentations where in-person observation provides little corresponding diagnostic advantage telemedicine could not adequately substitute.
options: Telemedicine Confirmed to Be Equally Effective Across Every Clinical Presentation Without Exception
Telemedicine's Value Varying by Clinical Presentation, Complicating Both Enthusiasm and Skepticism
In-Person Observation Found to Provide No Diagnostic Advantage for Any Mental Health Condition
Researchers Found Telemedicine Skepticism to Be Entirely Justified Across All Presentations
quests.correctAnswer: Telemedicine's Value Varying by Clinical Presentation, Complicating Both Enthusiasm and Skepticism
quests.hint: Compare the specific subset of clinical situations where telemedicine has genuine limitations with the larger set of situations where it works just as well, and how this nuanced picture challenges both overly positive and overly negative views.
quests.explanation: This passage unites genuine telemedicine benefits for most presentations with documented limitations for a specific subset requiring direct observation, explicitly complicating both uncritical enthusiasm and reflexive skepticism. The summary should capture that nuanced, presentation-dependent picture rather than endorse either extreme view.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Esports organizations' increasing adoption of structured practice regimens and sports psychology consultation, mirroring approaches long standard in traditional professional athletics, reflects a broader professionalization trend within competitive gaming that has produced documented performance improvements among teams adopting these practices. Researchers studying esports athlete wellbeing, though, have identified a parallel pattern of repetitive strain injury and burnout rates among professional players considerably higher than would be predicted from the activity's comparatively low physical exertion relative to traditional sports. This pattern is attributed to esports' unusually intensive, sustained fine-motor repetition, combined with a competitive culture that has, in adopting traditional sports' performance optimization techniques, been slower to simultaneously adopt the injury-prevention and recovery protocols traditional sports developed over a much longer institutional history. Esports, in other words, has selectively imported the performance-enhancing half of traditional sports science, while still developing the protective half at a comparatively earlier stage.
options: Esports Adopting Sports Science's Performance Half Faster Than Its Protective Half
Esports Organizations Confirmed to Have Fully Adopted Both Performance and Injury-Prevention Practices
Professional Gamers Found to Experience Lower Injury Rates Than Traditional Athletes
Researchers Found No Connection Between Esports' Practice Intensity and Injury Rates
quests.correctAnswer: Esports Adopting Sports Science's Performance Half Faster Than Its Protective Half
quests.hint: Weigh the two different categories of sports science practice distinguished, performance optimization and injury prevention, and which one esports organizations have adopted more quickly than the other.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Algorithmic playlist curation on music streaming platforms is designed to surface new music aligned with a listener's established preferences, based on listening history analysis, and has been credited by some industry observers with helping listeners discover music they would not have otherwise encountered through traditional radio or retail discovery channels. Musicologists studying genre evolution raise a more structural concern about long-term creative diversity, though. Since these algorithms are trained predominantly on historical listening patterns reflecting music that already exists and has already found an audience, they are structurally better suited to recommending variations within already-established genre conventions than to surfacing or encouraging genuinely novel musical approaches lacking sufficient existing listener data to generate confident algorithmic recommendation. This limitation, if algorithmic discovery comes to dominate how listeners encounter new music, could plausibly favor incremental genre evolution over the kind of discontinuous creative innovation that has historically driven major shifts in popular music, even though no definitive evidence yet confirms this specific long-term effect has actually occurred.
options: Algorithmic Curation Confirmed to Have Already Caused Measurable Decline in Musical Innovation
Algorithmic Discovery's Structural Bias Toward Convention, with an Unconfirmed Long-Term Risk
These Algorithms Found to Be Equally Capable of Surfacing Novel and Conventional Music
Musicologists Found Definitive Evidence Confirming This Long-Term Creative Effect Has Occurred
quests.correctAnswer: Algorithmic Discovery's Structural Bias Toward Convention, with an Unconfirmed Long-Term Risk
quests.hint: Notice the structural reason given for why these algorithms favor established genre conventions, and whether the passage claims this concern has already been proven to affect music or remains a plausible but unconfirmed risk.
quests.explanation: This passage combines a structural explanation for why algorithmic curation favors convention over genuine novelty with an explicit caveat that this remains a plausible but unconfirmed long-term risk rather than an established fact. The summary should preserve that careful epistemic distinction rather than overstate the finding as already proven.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Open-plan university dormitory designs are intended to encourage spontaneous social interaction among residents by minimizing physical barriers between individual living spaces and shared common areas. Research findings show this to be considerably more dependent on student personality and preference than the design philosophy's universal social-benefit framing typically acknowledges. Students with introverted temperaments or strong preferences for predictable solitude report measurably higher stress and lower overall housing satisfaction in open-plan environments, compared to otherwise similar students in more traditional, privacy-preserving dormitory layouts, while extroverted students or those strongly prioritizing social connection show the opposite pattern. A single dormitory design philosophy, however well-intentioned its social goals, cannot serve a genuinely diverse student population's varying needs equally well, a mismatch that has prompted some universities to offer multiple dormitory design options explicitly, rather than committing institution-wide to a single architectural philosophy presumed to benefit all residents similarly.
options: Open-Plan Dormitory Design Confirmed to Benefit All Students Equally Regardless of Personality
Introverted Students Found to Report Higher Satisfaction in Open-Plan Layouts
Dormitory Design Benefits Depending on Personality, Prompting a Shift to Multiple Options
Universities Found to Commit Exclusively to a Single Dormitory Design Philosophy
quests.correctAnswer: Dormitory Design Benefits Depending on Personality, Prompting a Shift to Multiple Options
quests.hint: Consider how the effect of open-plan dormitory design differs depending on a student's personality type, and what practical response some universities have adopted in light of that variation.
quests.explanation: This passage brings together contrasting outcomes for different personality types under the same dormitory design with universities' resulting move toward offering multiple design options rather than one universal approach. The summary should capture both that personality-dependent variation and the practical institutional response.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Workplace open-door policies, in which managers explicitly invite employees to raise concerns or ask questions at any time without needing a scheduled appointment, are frequently implemented with the sincere intention of increasing communication accessibility and reducing hierarchical distance between managers and staff. Organizational communication researchers studying actual employee behavior under such policies, though, have found that the policy's stated openness does not reliably translate into employees actually feeling comfortable utilizing it. Employees continue to make implicit judgments about appropriate timing and topic based on subtler cues, a manager's visible workload, body language, or general approachability in the moment, that the formal policy itself does nothing to address. A policy's official existence and an employee's actual felt psychological permission to use it, in other words, represent two distinct things that can diverge considerably, with the gap between them depending more on a manager's consistently demonstrated receptiveness over time than on the formal policy's stated terms.
options: Open-Door Policies Confirmed to Reliably Translate into Employees Feeling Comfortable Speaking Up
Employee Comfort Found to Depend Entirely on the Formal Policy's Stated Terms
Manager Behavior Found to Have No Influence on Whether Employees Use the Open-Door Policy
Open-Door Policies' Stated Openness Often Diverging from Employees' Actual Felt Permission
quests.correctAnswer: Open-Door Policies' Stated Openness Often Diverging from Employees' Actual Felt Permission
quests.hint: Think about the gap between a policy's official, stated openness and an employee's actual felt comfort using it, and what factor actually closes or widens that gap.
quests.explanation: This passage links the sincere intention behind open-door policies with research showing a persistent gap between stated and felt openness, attributing that gap to ongoing manager behavior rather than the formal policy itself. The summary should capture that distinction between formal policy and lived experience.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Standardized rubrics for evaluating student writing are designed to increase grading consistency across different teachers and reduce the subjective variability that unstructured holistic grading can introduce. They have demonstrated genuine success at their primary stated goal of improving inter-rater reliability: multiple teachers grading the same piece of writing now arrive at more similar scores than before rubric adoption. Writing researchers, though, have identified a less frequently discussed secondary effect. Students writing specifically to satisfy enumerated rubric criteria sometimes produce technically compliant but creatively constrained work that checks every required box while lacking the kind of distinctive voice or genuinely original approach that holistic evaluation, despite its greater subjectivity and lower inter-rater consistency, was sometimes better positioned to recognize and reward. Rubrics, in other words, may have resolved one genuine problem, grading inconsistency, while introducing a different, harder-to-measure cost to writing quality and creative risk-taking that the consistency improvement does not by itself offset.
options: Writing Rubrics Solving Grading Inconsistency While Introducing a Creativity Cost
Standardized Rubrics Confirmed to Improve Both Grading Consistency and Creative Writing Quality
Holistic Grading Found to Produce Less Consistent Scores Than Rubrics While Offering No Other Benefit
Writing Researchers Found No Connection Between Rubric Use and Constrained Student Writing
quests.correctAnswer: Writing Rubrics Solving Grading Inconsistency While Introducing a Creativity Cost
quests.hint: Look at the genuine problem rubrics successfully solve compared to the different, less obvious cost they may introduce regarding student creativity and originality.
quests.explanation: This passage connects the rubric's genuine success at improving grading consistency with a separate, harder-to-measure cost to creative writing quality that this consistency gain does not offset. The summary should capture both the real benefit and the real trade-off rather than present rubrics as a costless improvement.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Honeymoon destination trends, tracked by travel industry analysts through booking data over several decades, reveal a documented shift away from the once-dominant model of an extended, single-destination luxury resort stay, toward shorter, multi-destination itineraries combining distinct experiences. Analysts attribute this shift to several converging factors, including increased budget consciousness among younger couples carrying student debt unknown to previous generations at the same life stage, greater premium placed on curated, photogenic experiences shareable on social media relative to pure relaxation, and changing workplace norms around extended leave availability that have compressed typical honeymoon duration considerably compared to decades past. This multi-causal explanation complicates any single-factor account, whether purely economic or purely cultural, of why honeymoon travel patterns have changed as measurably as the booking data confirms they have.
options: Honeymoon Trends Shifting Through Several Converging Economic and Cultural Factors
Honeymoon Trends Confirmed to Have Remained Essentially Unchanged Across Decades
A Single Economic Factor Found to Fully Explain the Documented Shift in Travel Patterns
Booking Data Found to Show No Measurable Change in Honeymoon Destination Choices
quests.correctAnswer: Honeymoon Trends Shifting Through Several Converging Economic and Cultural Factors
quests.hint: Ask yourself about the several different factors contributing to the shift in honeymoon travel patterns, noticing that no single factor is presented as the complete explanation.
quests.explanation: This passage pairs multiple converging factors, budget consciousness, social media culture, and workplace leave norms, into a multi-causal explanation for documented changes in honeymoon travel patterns. The summary should capture that combined, multi-factor explanation rather than attribute the shift to any single cause.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Multigenerational family vacation planning, in which grandparents, parents, and grandchildren travel together to a shared destination, requires reconciling activity preferences and physical capability ranges considerably wider than typical single-generation travel planning must accommodate. Destination researchers studying this growing travel segment note that this planning challenge has prompted measurable shifts in how certain resort and cruise operators structure their offerings, including expanded simultaneous programming across distinct age-appropriate activity tracks operating in parallel rather than sequentially. This allows different generations to pursue separately suited activities during overlapping time blocks, before reconvening for shared meals or evening activities. Several operators report that this structural accommodation has driven measurable growth in multigenerational bookings specifically, suggesting that addressing this particular planning challenge through deliberate parallel programming, rather than expecting one shared itinerary to satisfy every generation simultaneously, has become a genuine competitive differentiator within this expanding segment.
options: Multigenerational Travel Operators Confirmed to Rely on a Single Shared Itinerary for All Ages
Parallel Activity Programming Becoming a Competitive Edge in Multigenerational Travel
Parallel Programming Found to Have Caused a Decline in Multigenerational Bookings
Destination Researchers Found No Connection Between Programming Structure and Booking Growth
quests.correctAnswer: Parallel Activity Programming Becoming a Competitive Edge in Multigenerational Travel
quests.hint: Identify the specific structural solution some operators developed to address the challenge of planning for multiple generations with different needs, and what business result that solution has produced.
quests.explanation: This passage weaves together the genuine planning challenge multigenerational travel presents with a specific structural solution, parallel programming, that operators report has driven measurable booking growth. The summary should capture that solution and its competitive business effect rather than suggest a single shared itinerary remains standard or that the new approach failed.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Family heirloom transmission is the practice of passing specific physical objects, jewelry, furniture, tools, down through successive generations as carriers of family memory and identity. It faces a documented generational shift in reception that sociologists studying material culture attribute to several interacting factors, rather than to younger generations simply valuing family history less than their predecessors did. Younger recipients report genuine appreciation for family history and connection, but cite practical constraints including smaller living spaces less able to accommodate bulky furniture, greater residential mobility complicating the long-term storage of numerous heirloom objects, and a general cultural shift toward valuing experiences and digital memory preservation over accumulated physical possessions. Declining heirloom retention, in other words, reflects a complex interaction between persistent emotional valuation and changed practical life circumstances, rather than representing any straightforward generational decline in caring about family history or continuity.
options: Younger Generations Confirmed to Value Family History Significantly Less Than Predecessors
Declining Heirloom Retention Found to Stem Purely from a Lack of Emotional Attachment
Heirloom Decline Reflecting Practical Constraints, Not Reduced Care About Family History
Practical Living Constraints Found to Have No Influence on Heirloom Retention Decisions
quests.correctAnswer: Heirloom Decline Reflecting Practical Constraints, Not Reduced Care About Family History
quests.hint: Focus on the passage's explicit distinction between younger generations' actual emotional valuation of family history and the practical constraints that separately affect whether they keep physical heirloom objects.
quests.explanation: This passage draws together persistent emotional valuation of family history with separate practical constraints like space and mobility to explain declining heirloom retention, explicitly rejecting a simple generational-decline-in-caring narrative. The summary should capture that nuanced, multi-factor explanation rather than confirm reduced caring as the cause.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Food irradiation is a preservation technique using controlled doses of ionizing radiation to eliminate harmful bacteria and extend shelf life, without the chemical residue associated with some alternative preservation methods. It has been repeatedly evaluated by major food safety regulatory bodies and found to pose no detectable health risk to consumers at approved treatment levels. This scientific consensus has nonetheless failed to translate into widespread consumer acceptance or commercial adoption in many markets. Food science communication researchers attribute this gap partly to the technique's name itself, since 'irradiation' carries strong associative connections to nuclear weapons and radioactive contamination in public imagination that bear little technical relationship to the actual, well-understood food safety mechanism involved. This illustrates a broader pattern in which a technology's public reception can diverge substantially from its actual scientific risk profile, based largely on linguistic and associative framing rather than on any genuine disagreement about the underlying technical evidence.
options: Public Rejection of Food Irradiation Confirmed to Reflect Genuine, Unresolved Scientific Safety Concerns
Regulatory Bodies Found to Have Identified Significant Health Risks from Approved Irradiation Levels
The Gap Between Acceptance and Safety Consensus Found to Stem from Technical Disagreement Among Scientists
Food Irradiation's Safety Consensus Undermined by Linguistic Associations, Not Evidence Disputes
quests.correctAnswer: Food Irradiation's Safety Consensus Undermined by Linguistic Associations, Not Evidence Disputes
quests.hint: Picture whether the gap between scientific consensus and public acceptance of food irradiation stems from a genuine technical dispute or from something else related to the technology's name.
quests.explanation: This passage balances a strong scientific safety consensus on food irradiation against persistently low public acceptance, attributing that gap specifically to linguistic and associative framing around the word 'irradiation' rather than genuine technical disagreement. The summary should capture that specific framing-based explanation.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Personalized nutrition recommendations generated from analysis of an individual's gut microbiome composition are marketed as offering more precisely tailored dietary guidance than generic population-level nutrition advice. They rest on a genuinely active and evolving area of scientific research, showing real associations between specific microbiome compositions and individual variation in metabolic responses to certain foods. Nutrition scientists caution, though, that current commercial applications of this research have generally outpaced the science's actual current predictive maturity, since the field has not yet established the kind of robust, consistently replicated causal mechanisms and validated predictive models that would be necessary to support the highly specific, individualized dietary prescriptions some commercial services confidently provide to paying customers. A genuinely promising area of active scientific inquiry, in other words, is currently being commercially marketed with a degree of confident specificity that the underlying research, however legitimate and actively progressing, does not yet actually substantiate.
options: Commercial Microbiome Nutrition Services Confirmed to Rest on Fully Validated Predictive Models
The Underlying Microbiome Research Found to Be Entirely Illegitimate and Without Merit
Microbiome Nutrition Commerce Outpacing What the Underlying Science Currently Supports
Nutrition Scientists Found No Gap Between Commercial Claims and Current Research Maturity
quests.correctAnswer: Microbiome Nutrition Commerce Outpacing What the Underlying Science Currently Supports
quests.hint: Compare the genuine, legitimate scientific research on microbiome and nutrition with the specific, confident claims some commercial services make based on that research.
quests.explanation: This passage unites genuinely promising, legitimate microbiome research with a caution that commercial applications have outpaced the science's actual current predictive maturity. The summary should capture that specific gap between legitimate ongoing research and premature commercial overconfidence, rather than dismiss the research entirely or accept commercial claims at face value.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Online grocery delivery services, having expanded substantially to serve customers seeking to avoid in-person shopping trips, depend on personal shoppers who select specific items on a customer's behalf from store shelves. This substitution process introduces a documented quality consistency challenge absent from in-person shopping, since produce selection in particular, choosing ripe but not overripe fruit, avoiding bruised vegetables, involves tactile and visual judgment that varies considerably between individual shoppers. Customers report experiencing this inconsistently across different orders, even when ordering the identical product from the identical store. This variability has prompted some delivery services to implement more detailed selection guidelines and shopper training specifically targeting produce selection, with measurable but still incomplete success at closing the consistency gap between trained professional shoppers' selections and what an attentive customer would have selected personally. Certain categories of shopping judgment, it seems, remain genuinely difficult to standardize across different individual shoppers even with deliberate training investment.
options: Produce Selection Variability Persisting Despite Delivery Services' Shopper Training Efforts
Personal Shopper Training Confirmed to Have Fully Eliminated Produce Selection Variability
Produce Selection Judgment Found to Require No Tactile or Visual Skill at All
Customers Found to Experience Fully Consistent Produce Quality Across Every Delivery Order
quests.correctAnswer: Produce Selection Variability Persisting Despite Delivery Services' Shopper Training Efforts
quests.hint: Weigh the specific challenge identified with produce selection in grocery delivery, what services have done to address it, and how complete or incomplete that solution actually is.
quests.explanation: This passage ties together the documented produce selection variability problem with delivery services' training-based response, explicitly noting that response has achieved only measurable but incomplete success. The summary should capture that partial, ongoing limitation rather than suggest the problem has been fully solved or that selection requires no real skill.
